findings_to_judge.claim: The syndicated Q1 FY27 consensus revenue of $9.47bn (+10.4% on the $8,578m year-ago base) sits roughly a point below what Medtronic's own 3 June quarterly guidance implies — 11.5% to 12.0% organic growth plus a 'neutral to $50 million' FX tailwind plus acquired revenue from CathWorks/Scientia/SPR, i.e. about $9.55-9.65bn — while consensus EPS of $1.39 is exactly the midpoint of the guided $1.38-$1.40; the same one-point gap exists at the full-year level ($38.85bn consensus vs 6.75-7.25% organic on $36,364m plus 0-1% FX plus M&A). The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management sized at 500-600bps of Q1 revenue but 600-700bps of Q1 EPS, so the EPS line was captured and part of the revenue line was not. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.

As of 2026-08-31 no registration statement or tender-offer document for the MiniMed split-off exists on EDGAR: Medtronic (CIK 1613103) has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-03 and no S-4/Schedule TO, and MiniMed Group (CIK 2062583) shows no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO on or after 2026-06-01. On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. An exchange offer needs a registered offer document and a ~20-business-day offer period, so with nothing on file at end-August the 'upside from early separation' has not begun to be executed. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.

The Investor Day Medtronic committed to on 2025-08-19, when it added two Elliott-adjacent directors and formed the Growth and Operating Committees, was promised for 'mid-calendar year 2026' and was to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the committees' margin and efficiency targets. Mid-2026 has passed and, as of 2026-08-31, no date has been announced: the June Q4 call did not mention it and the Medtronic newsroom shows only three releases since (21 July Touch Surgery Aide, 6 August Affera CE Mark, 20 August dividend).

Boston Scientific reported on 2026-07-29 that its electrophysiology business grew only 3% in the US in calendar Q2 2026 (versus 23% internationally), citing competitive pressure and noting that US PFA is now roughly 80% of the AFib market. Calendar Q2 covers about two-thirds of Medtronic's fiscal Q1 (25 April to 31 July), and Cardiac Ablation Solutions — up 78% globally and 124% in the US in Medtronic's Q4 FY26 — is the single largest contributor to the 6.75-7.25% FY27 organic guide. The datapoint reads as continued Affera/Sphere-9 share gain in the quarter Medtronic is about to report, but the same disclosure caps how much market growth is left.
